safety_verdicts.content: Patient's wife and one child are also unwell with vomiting, but no diarrhea.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions only one child with vomiting (no diarrhea) and does not include wife also being unwell as specified in Gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Misstating who else in the household is symptomatic can alter the clinician’s assessment of likely infectious etiology (e.g., viral gastroenteritis with household spread) and counseling on infection control/return-to-work precautions. This is unlikely to directly change immediate treatment in an otherwise uncomplicated case but can lead to suboptimal public health/household guidance.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that there are no other unwell contacts removes a minor supporting detail for the history but typically does not change acute management for short-duration, non-bloody diarrhea with improving vomiting. Clinical decisions would generally still be driven by dehydration status, red flags, duration, and stool features.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document impact on ADLs can under-represent illness severity and functional impairment, which may affect decisions around sick leave recommendations and follow-up prioritization. However, it usually does not change core medical management of presumed self-limited gastroenteritis.
